# Ariadne

> Ariadne is a local-first multilingual memory server for Codex, Claude Code, and any MCP client.

## Core facts

- Project site: https://mclaut.github.io/ariadne/
- Hugging Face Space: https://huggingface.co/spaces/mclaut/ariadne
- Source and documentation: https://github.com/mclaut/ariadne
- Latest release: https://github.com/mclaut/ariadne/releases/latest
- License: MIT
- Platforms: Windows x64, macOS Intel and Apple Silicon, Linux x64 and ARM64
- Runtime: Go MCP server, Qdrant vector server, Ollama bge-m3 embeddings
- Retrieval: exact lookup by ID or hybrid dense plus BM25 sparse search, with wing, room, and collection scopes plus bounded historical-intent reranking
- MCP tools: memory_save, memory_recall, memory_delete, memory_move, credential_access
- Privacy: local endpoints by default; Qdrant binds to 127.0.0.1; project scope is default-deny; cross-wing recall requires a visible human approval
- Lifecycle: scoped append-only identities retain superseded and orphaned history for exact-ID audit
- Maintenance: incremental memfile sync, JSON-only guarded diary consolidation, bounded retries, a 20-minute child deadline, and append-only health activity
- Token efficiency: measured savings, estimated legacy attribution, unattributed recall delivery, and signed net are reported separately without storing content

## Install

Windows uses install.ps1. Linux and macOS use install.sh. Both are available in the repository root.

## Upgrade compatibility

Trays running v0.8.14 or newer update normally after explicit user confirmation. A tray still running v0.8.13 or older may hit the old update-handoff bug and needs one pinned upgrade: `curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mclaut/ariadne/v0.8.16/install.sh | sh`. This reuses existing Qdrant data, backups, settings, and logs. Once v0.8.16 is active, later confirmed tray updates keep `Ariadne.app`, the tray, and command-line binaries synchronized.

## Current release

v0.8.25 uses one independently restored full recovery set when an explicit full-backup plan is configured. Runtime, client configuration and collection snapshots are included in that set instead of accumulating separately. Existing extra copies require a separately approved cleanup plan. Audit, manifests and recovery logs remain outside rotation.

v0.8.18 makes the access-request menu readable: pending decisions appear in a separate active queue near the top of the tray, and retained history is paginated ten records at a time, newest first. Purpose and short status labels appear in each row; exact scope, resource, creation time, and ID are in details. Active actions remain bound to one request ID; reusable history slots are strictly read-only. Every audit record is preserved. The existing explicit MCP approval retry and grant deadlines remain unchanged.

v0.8.17 adds a complete tray access-request queue and retained history with pending, approved, denied, expired, and consumed statuses. Exact-ID controls avoid acting on a changing queue head. Per-request cooldowns and 30-second dialogs rotate prompts fairly. Approval explicitly requires a client retry with approval_id; one-time credential grants reject reuse. `ariadnectl approvals --all` reads every retained lifecycle without authorizing access. Request records, decisions, and consumptions are preserved.

v0.8.16 adds a signed macOS `Ariadne.app` with a native icon to Applications. Launching it from Finder, Spotlight, or Launchpad starts the managed tray LaunchAgent and re-registers its canonical plist when needed without creating an unmanaged duplicate. It also keeps the macOS-only launcher tests out of Windows CI while preserving a Windows-safe launcher stub in release archives.

v0.8.12 adds owner-approved persistent credential trust for one exact source wing, target wing, resource, and purpose; every use, trust, and revocation remains append-only. It also explicitly disables Ollama thinking for schema-bound consolidation JSON and gives the maintenance supervisor a 20-minute default deadline, so an unresponsive child cannot leave scheduled maintenance stuck for hours. v0.8.11 guarantees one desktop tray through a Unix file lock or Windows named mutex, reconciles canonical and historical macOS launchd jobs on every install, archives superseded plist files without deletion, and teaches doctor to count actual tray processes. v0.8.10 makes attribution auditable: Qdrant pagination preserves unsigned 64-bit offsets exactly, corpus coverage separates recallable memory from inactive or security-excluded history, measured source provenance remains distinct from conservative legacy estimates, remaining diary/consolidation/manual gaps are explicit, and attribution backfill is read-only until `--apply`. v0.8.9 prevents Qdrant file-descriptor exhaustion under many concurrent MCP sessions: each process uses one gRPC connection, macOS launchd grants 8192 descriptors, startup creates only missing payload indexes, clients close cleanly, and status/tray/doctor report descriptor pressure. v0.8.8 adds fail-closed remote Qdrant API-key/TLS policy, append-only metrics v3 daily rollups and indexed recent reads, complete paginated collection reconciliation, deterministic judged BM25-versus-learned-sparse evaluation, reusable maintenance retries, and reversible site cleanup. v0.8.7 verified Start, Stop, and Restart by observing Qdrant and Ollama state and PIDs, requiring a green collection before success, resolving Homebrew under launchd's restricted PATH, attempting recovery after partial stop failures, and delivering completion from the replacement tray through an append-only notification journal. v0.8.6 added deliberate Approve/Deny prompts and persistent Claude recall across context transitions. v0.8.3 introduced scoped cross-wing and separate one-shot credential grants, while v0.8.2 made project scope default-deny and added secret blocking plus append-only quarantine. The approval handshake is audited agent policy, not an operating-system credential broker.

Full backup rotation: a private explicit plan retains one independently verified full recovery set. Audit is retained outside rotation. See https://github.com/mclaut/ariadne/blob/main/docs/backup-full.md

Runtime rotation v0.8.24: legacy release-local previous-runtime copies join canonical retention after independent runtime recovery; audit metadata and retired-file inventories are preserved.

Version 0.8.32 judges the consolidation curator's language by prose rather than code: code spans, URLs and identifier-like tokens no longer make a Ukrainian diary full of commands look English, and the language check, the prompt hint and the repair guidance name the same language, so such batches are no longer set aside on every run. A language deferral names the expected and the actual language, and earlier deferrals are reconsidered once.

Version 0.8.31 keeps the tray calm: a deferred consolidation from the previous run is no longer reported as a maintenance failure when the next run starts, and the tray changes its dot color or notifies only after two consecutive polls agree. When the consolidation quality gate rejects a candidate set, each candidate is judged alone and the set only for duplicates; a candidate that mixes independent facts is split into separate memories, and earlier deferrals are reconsidered once.

Version 0.8.30 adds the Ariadne panel: a loopback-only, token-protected local page opened from the tray or Ariadne.app that explains why the tray dot is yellow or red, with service state, recent maintenance, log tails and controls; tray color changes are logged with reasons. Failed or interrupted full backups no longer leave their unpublished stage behind, and consolidation uses qwen2.5:14b when it is installed and no model is configured.

Version 0.8.29 keeps Qdrant running through updates (the installer waits for launchd to release a service before restarting it and retries the start) and drains the whole consolidation queue in one run: no run-wide deadline, transient Ollama failures retried in place, each group saved as it finishes, and timed-out batches no longer deferred for the pipeline revision.

Version 0.8.28 fixes tray updates and fresh installs that failed with a Go checksum mismatch (the bootstrap now verifies Go from dl.google.com) and reports maintenance cut short by a system restart as interrupted rather than stuck.

Version 0.8.27 is a security maintenance release: binaries are built with Go 1.26.11 (24 reachable standard-library advisories closed), golang.org/x/net v0.63.0 and gRPC v1.85.0, and CI plus every release run govulncheck so a reachable vulnerability blocks the build. No data, configuration or behavior changes.

Version 0.8.26 surfaced failed backups independently of maintenance progress, warned during retries, and sent notifications for each new failed attempt. Explicit preserving repair mode retains previous full and verification copies; recovery checks remain mandatory.
